about: Stop 1 dive, re-roll: the camera rises over the glass, looks straight down, follows the scoop's powder down into the water and keeps looking down as it blooms, so no floating layer is ever seen from below.

input.prompt: A glass of clear water on a nightstand, a hand holding a heaped scoop of fine green powder just above it. The camera rises smoothly over the glass and tilts to look straight down into it from above, following the scoop as the hand tips it: the green powder pours away from us, down into the water. The camera then plunges straight down after the falling powder, through the water's surface, and keeps looking downward as it sinks: below and around us the green powder bursts into soft, swirling plumes that spread and dissolve, with warm morning light shining down through the water from above. We never look back up at the surface. Ends deep inside the glowing, softly green water, the plumes fading into an even green. Realistic, moody photograph in motion, continuing exactly from this frame: first light in a quiet bedroom, low warm sun through linen curtains, deep soft shadows, fine film grain, shot on a 35mm lens. First-person point of view, one smooth, continuous, gimbal-like movement, no shake, no cut. The hand wears a soft plain grey long-sleeved sleep shirt. No face, no other person, no head or hair at the edges of the frame, no mirror, no text overlay.
